# vk 0.8.0 — direct allocator concurrency

Development release, 2026-10-29. Cargo package **`vkrust 0.8.0+1.4.365`**,
Rust library/import name **`vk`**, Git tag **`v0.8.0`**, MIT licensed.
The `+1.4.365` suffix identifies the unchanged pinned Vulkan header snapshot;
it is not a Vulkan 1.4 driver requirement.

[Developer guide](https://dev.realm.software/vk) ·
[Rust API reference](https://docs.rs/vkrust/latest/vk/) ·
[Realm](https://realm.software/)

## API and migration

This is a minor API release: `SynchronizedAllocator` gains direct `&self`
operations and `SynchronizedVirtualBlock` is added in `vk::mem` and re-exported
at the crate root. Existing `Allocator`, Vulkan operations, raw ABI declarations,
borrowed record construction and allocator free functions keep their contracts.
Use Cargo requirement `version = "0.8"` with feature `allocator` for memory APIs.
Existing scoped `with_allocator`, `with_pools`, `with_memory_types` and
`with_blocks` remain available; no process-global allocator or dispatch is added.

The synchronized owner retains its unsafe any-thread adoption contract for
callbacks, borrowed native chains, external references and mapped storage.
Direct map/unmap/bind methods reserve a live allocation and pending resource
claim, then execute under a stable per-backing mutex without the placement
mutex. Allocation/free on other backings in the same pool can proceed while
one native call blocks. Regions on one backing serialize native map/bind work
and preserve explicit/persistent mapping counts and cache state.

Backing promotion fallibly reserves callback-owned CPU storage before native
effects and preserves pre-existing maps on failure. Target retirement waits for
its lease; global services, borrowed access and relocation wait for active
native calls. Nonblocking access reports busy. Errors retain retry ownership;
panic poisons access and consuming recovery retains the native owner without
certifying an interrupted transaction. Native cleanup remains explicit.

`SynchronizedVirtualBlock` provides optional mutex-protected host-only placement,
checked tokens, callback-backed construction/adoption and poison recovery. Pinned
VMA 3.4.0 itself requires external synchronization of virtual blocks; this
wrapper is a Rust convenience. Standard-library synchronization/runtime storage
follows platform allocation policy. No host lock protects escaped mapped bytes
or establishes GPU completion, and Drop performs no Vulkan cleanup.

## Documentation and discovery

The README uses the VK developer cover, with the Realm animation above License.
The crate homepage points to the VK developer guide; docs.rs remains the Rust
API documentation URL. README links expose both Realm and developer resources.
Internal incremental verification reports are consolidated into one allocator
summary; Git history retains the detailed checkpoints. Public qualification
continues to live in the [qualification report](../qualification.md).

## Evidence and limits

The allocator source/test checkpoint passed 3,438 Rust tests/doctests, including
50 generator cases; the final runtime rerun and actual extracted archive each
passed 3,388 cases. Fifty Python tooling tests, strict Clippy, minimal/default
feature tests, Windows-GNU cross-Clippy, deterministic generation, strict rustdoc
and public package consumers passed. Release CI reruns the configured tests,
package/consumer checks and pinned-header oracles on this release's exact public
snapshot; its artifacts record the release archive and toolchain identity.

Rust ASan passed 332 library/memory cases with leak detection; TSan passed 22
threading and 46 memory integration cases with the standard library rebuilt
under matching instrumentation. Both reported zero diagnostics. System/driver
libraries remain uninstrumented; standard library is not ASan-instrumented in
this profile. These are scoped sanitizer results, not universal race freedom.

Pinned VMA 3.4.0 commit `3aa921224c154a0d2c43912bc88e1c42ce1f7607`
passed 12 independent concurrency comparisons, 1,024 native-model and 56 virtual
traces (868,344 operations), and 1,600 memory preference cases. C++ ASan/UBSan
reported zero diagnostics. Each implementation independently satisfies bounds,
placement, mapping, failure, accounting and cleanup checks; agreement alone
cannot make a bad outcome pass. Deliberate policy differences and scoped donor
regressions remain explicit.

Seven real-device profiles passed under each of separate core/thread-safety and
synchronization/thread-safety validation: 14 passes, no runtime skips or validation
errors/warnings/VUIDs/hazards. Hardware was Intel HD Graphics 4400 (Haswell GT2),
Mesa 26.2.5, Vulkan 1.2.354, granularity one and atom size 64. Profiles cover
direct and scoped host buffer work, independent backings, opaque-FD/DMA-BUF
buffer imports and opaque-FD linear-image imports. Mesa's separate warning about
incomplete Haswell support is retained. Only one native host-visible memory type
is qualified; independent two-type overlap uses synthetic gates.

The allocator remains Experimental. Direct placement is serialized per owner;
pool/type scopes provide independent placement owners. Full VMA policy/service
and stress equivalence, native relocation-copy correctness, broader platform
imports/GPU handoff and comparative performance remain unqualified. Non-coherent,
granularity-greater-than-one, positive device-address/device-group and Vulkan
1.3/1.4 physical workloads need additional hardware evidence. Cross-compilation
is not native Windows qualification. No fastest, full parity or production
readiness claim follows from this release.
